behaviour: Pure helpers that resolve a wizard step's JSON Schema against the accumulated answers of all steps, so a condition in step N can reference an answer from an earlier step, and that report which answers have become unreachable.
rules: Declare a module-local `function isObject(value: unknown): value is JsonObject` exactly as lib/schema.ts does. Do not import one.
Declare a module-local `const validator = customizeValidator();` at module scope, from '@rjsf/validator-ajv8'. Build it once per module, never per call.
Import `retrieveSchema` from '@rjsf/utils'. It is exported from that package's root.

`collectGoverningKeys(stepSchema)`: return the set of property names a step's conditions test. Collect every key of `stepSchema.dependencies` when it is an object. When `stepSchema.if` is an object, collect every key of `if.properties` when that is an object, and every string entry of `if.required` when that is an array. Recurse into `then`, `else`, and each object entry of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, and into each object value of `dependencies`, collecting their `dependencies` keys and `if` keys the same way. Never collect a plain `properties` key as governing.

`collectConditionalPropertyNames(stepSchema)`: return the set of property names declared ONLY inside conditional subschemas. Walk `dependencies` values, `if`, `then`, `else`, and each object entry of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, recursively; at every node BELOW the root collect the keys of that node's `properties` when it is an object. Never collect the keys of the root's own `properties`.

`pickConditionData(stepSchema, formState)`: return a new plain object holding, for each key of `collectGoverningKeys(stepSchema)`, that key's value from `formState` when `formState` has it as an own property. Omit any key `formState` lacks. Never include a key that is not governing.

`resolveStepSchema(stepSchema, formState)` returns the SAME `stepSchema` reference, with no copying, when any of: `stepSchema` is not an object; it has no object `dependencies` and no object `if`; it has no own object `properties` key (RJSF already resolves a dependencies-only step correctly, so leave it alone); or every governing key is already a key of its own `properties`.

Otherwise `resolveStepSchema` computes, for each governing dependency key NOT in its own `properties`, an isolated probe `{ type: 'object', properties: { [key]: {} }, dependencies: { [key]: stepSchema.dependencies[key] } }`, calls `retrieveSchema(validator, probe, probe, formState)`, and takes from the outcome every `properties` entry except the probe's own stub key, plus every `required` entry except that stub key.

When `stepSchema.if` is an object and at least one of its governing keys is absent from the step's own `properties`, resolve it with one further probe `{ type: 'object', properties: <a stub {} per absent governing key>, if: stepSchema.if, then: stepSchema.then, else: stepSchema.else }`, include `then`/`else` only when each is present, and take from the outcome every property and required entry except the stub keys.

The returned schema is a shallow copy of `stepSchema` with: `properties` set to the step's own properties followed by the collected additions (an addition never overwrites an own property of the same name); `required` set to the step's own `required` entries followed by the collected additions, de-duplicated, and the `required` key deleted entirely when that list is empty; each consumed cross-step dependency key removed from `dependencies`, and the `dependencies` key deleted when nothing is left in it; and `if`, `then`, `else` deleted when the `if` probe ran. Never mutate `stepSchema` or anything reachable from it.
`pruneUnreachableFormState(stepSchemas, formState)` returns the SAME `formState` reference whenever it would drop nothing, including when no step declares a conditional property.

A key is dropped by `pruneUnreachableFormState` only when all of: it is in the union of `collectConditionalPropertyNames` over every step; it is NOT a top-level `properties` key of ANY step (a key any step declares at top level is a real answer and always survives); it is absent from the `properties` of EVERY step's `resolveStepSchema(step, formState)` under the current state; and `formState` has it as an own property. Dropping otherwise is a defect.
When at least one key is dropped, return a new shallow copy of `formState` without those keys. Never delete a key from the argument.

No helper throws for any input. A governing key answered in no step yields no additions and no drops. A malformed subschema (a string, null, an array where an object is expected) is skipped, not an error.
No helper logs, and none deep-clones a whole step schema or the manifest.

style_from.reason: The house shape for a pure JSON Schema walker in this package: module-local isObject type guard, named export function, recursion over properties/items/anyOf/oneOf/allOf/dependencies/then/else, TSDoc with an @alpha tag on each export.

uses.reason: Shows how this package imports JsonObject/JsonValue and constructs schema tooling at module scope; the resolved schema this module returns is what gets handed to createAsyncValidators.

behaviour: Unit tests for the cross-step resolution helpers, covering the mobile-SDK shape from the originating issue, the additive-identity guarantees, and the unanswered-key case.
rules: Import the helpers relatively from './conditionalSchema'. No package-scoped self-import.
Build step schemas as inline literals typed `JsonObject`, shaped like a scaffolder step: `{ type: 'object', properties: { ... }, dependencies: { ... } }`.

The mobile-SDK fixture is two steps: step 1 declares `mobile` as a boolean; step 2 declares its own `repo` string and a `dependencies.mobile.oneOf` whose first branch adds `sdkName` with `required: ['sdkName']` under `mobile: { const: true }` and whose second branch is `mobile: { const: false }`.

Assert identity with `toBe` where a rule promises the same reference, and value with `toEqual` where it promises a resolved shape. `toBe` is the point of the additive-identity cases; `toEqual` there would pass vacuously.
Group the cases with `describe` per exported helper, following this package's test files.

style_from.reason: The colocated pure-module test idiom for this exact directory: plain describe/it, inline JsonObject literals, no React or test-app harness.

tests.name: resolveStepSchema surfaces a cross-step dependency field when the earlier answer satisfies it
tests.given: The mobile-SDK step 2, resolved against `{ mobile: true, repo: 'r' }`
tests.expect: The result's properties hold `repo` and `sdkName`, its required list holds `sdkName`, and it no longer carries a `dependencies` key; the input step schema object is unchanged

tests.name: resolveStepSchema omits the field and its required entry when the earlier answer does not satisfy the condition
tests.given: The same step 2 resolved against `{ mobile: false, repo: 'r' }`
tests.expect: The result's properties hold only `repo`, and the result has no `required` key and no `dependencies` key

tests.name: resolveStepSchema treats a governing key answered in no step as not holding and does not throw
tests.given: The same step 2 resolved against `{ repo: 'r' }`, and a step whose dependency names a key no step declares
tests.expect: Neither call throws; both results hold only the step's own properties and no added required entry

tests.name: resolveStepSchema resolves a root-level if/then that references an earlier step's answer
tests.given: A step with own `repo`, `if: { properties: { mobile: { const: true } }, required: ['mobile'] }` and `then` adding a required `sdkName`, resolved against `{ mobile: true }` and then `{ mobile: false }`
tests.expect: The first result holds `sdkName` and requires it; the second holds only `repo`, requires nothing, and neither result carries `if`, `then` or `else`

tests.name: resolveStepSchema resolves a dependency whose branch only adds required entries
tests.given: A step declaring both `repo` and `sdkName` in its own properties with `dependencies: { mobile: ['sdkName'] }`, resolved against `{ mobile: true }`
tests.expect: The result requires `sdkName` while its properties are unchanged

tests.name: resolveStepSchema returns the identical object for a step with no cross-step condition
tests.given: A step with no conditions; a step whose dependency key is declared in its own properties (a same-step condition); and a step with dependencies but no properties key
tests.expect: Each call returns the very object passed in, asserted with toBe

tests.name: pruneUnreachableFormState drops only the answer whose governing condition stopped holding
tests.given: The two mobile-SDK steps and `{ mobile: false, repo: 'r', sdkName: 's' }`
tests.expect: The result is `{ mobile: false, repo: 'r' }` — `sdkName` gone, the governing `mobile` and the unconditional `repo` kept

tests.name: pruneUnreachableFormState keeps a conditional answer while its condition still holds and returns the identical state when nothing is unreachable
tests.given: The same steps with `{ mobile: true, repo: 'r', sdkName: 's' }`, then two steps with no conditions at all and a state holding both their answers
tests.expect: The first result equals the input state; the second returns the very object passed in, asserted with toBe

tests.name: pickConditionData copies only the keys a step's conditions test
tests.given: A step whose `dependencies` names `mobile`, and one whose `if` names `mobile` via properties and required, against `{ mobile: true, repo: 'r', unrelated: 1 }`
tests.expect: Both results are `{ mobile: true }`; a state lacking `mobile` yields `{}` for both and neither call throws

behaviour: Re-export the new cross-step resolution helpers from the lib barrel so they reach the package's /alpha entry point.
rules: Add one explicit named re-export statement after the existing one. Keep `export *` out of this file.
Export exactly `resolveStepSchema`, `pruneUnreachableFormState` and `pickConditionData` from './conditionalSchema'.
Do not touch the Apache header or its year.

sites.rule: Append the new named re-export from './conditionalSchema' on the lines after this one, matching this file's single-line-per-module style.
